correctness.rationale: The result holds for the stated exchange-symmetric deterministic ODE on strictly positive initial states. Bounded interaction terms and logistic comparison give positive global solutions. Subtracting resident per-capita growth rates gives y′=−(a/2)p y(1−y²), and differencing invader and mean resident payoffs gives z′=zp[(−k+ar/2)p−dz]. Thus in ds=p dt the squared contrast obeys r_s=−ar(1−r) and the resident odds obey w_s+(−k+ar/2)w=d. Their integrating factor is H(s)=e^{cs}/√(r₀+(1−r₀)e^{as}); its integral is exactly T(r₀) by u=e^(−as). The numerator w₀+d∫H is strictly decreasing, and its limit distinguishes all three cases, with w₀=R/I. If the limit is positive or zero, s goes to infinity in physical time; on equality the tail ratio ∫_s^∞H/H tends to 1/k and yields w→−d/k. On these branches the eventual mean interaction tends respectively to a/2 and c(−d)/(k−d), so scalar logistic comparison gives the claimed positive total limits. When the numerator vanishes first at finite s*, w_s(s*)=d<0 and p has a simple zero there. Physical time diverges logarithmically; equivalently d(log p)/dt→d<0, giving integrability of the mean interaction Φ=O(p). Solving (1/N)′=μ−Φ/N and applying the Cesàro limit to its integrating factor yields μtN→1 and z→1. Differentiation gives T′>0. Substitution u=(1−r)v gives the beta constant by dominated convergence with dominating integrand v^(q−1)/√(1+v/2) for r≥1/2 and 0<q<1/2. The balanced threshold uses T(0)=1/k, and the resident-equilibrium rare-invader exponent is −k.

evidence: Under the stated parameters the rare-invader exponent at the resident equilibrium equals c−a/2<0. The primary model paper reports total extinction as one simulated outcome.

The frozen calculation determines the zero-terminal-numerator curve of a linear odds equation and derives the beta singularity; in physical time, integrable mean interaction is what gives the exact inverse-time mass prefactor.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Knowing the two qualitative facts does not mechanically give the absolute inoculum threshold at unequal resident densities or the cutoff-free time asymptotic. The latter follows from the crowding equation once the supercritical composition limit and decay are established and is not credited as new in isolation.

value.rationale: Within this published deterministic model class the finding quantifies the gap between linear invasion fitness and the actual basin. It provides a benchmark that is uniform over all positive initial triples in the symmetric slice, not a comparison of selected trajectories: the same resident sum can have arbitrarily different critical fractions as the imbalance changes, and asymptotic composition dominance is distinguished from establishment at positive abundance. The motivation and use are mathematical and model-specific.
